subject.title: ci: harden HTTP and local-auth gates against transient failures

question: Should the local-auth fix first preserve current shard sizing while measuring actual runner quota, or approve a runner-capacity change alongside retry and query reductions?
rationale: The reliability defect is well supported, but CI cost, provider-capacity expectations, and whether the work remains one umbrella or becomes two implementation tracks require repository-owner intent.

options.title: Measure, Then Split
options.body: Add temporary capacity and timeout diagnostics first, then pursue separate HTTP-fixture and local-auth-load changes based on measured evidence.

options.title: Increase Capacity Now
options.body: Move the heavy shards to a larger or different runner while retaining follow-up work to remove retry and query amplification.

options.title: Only Reduce Test Load
options.body: Keep runner allocation unchanged and address navigation retries, subscriptions, and timeout reporting without provider-capacity changes.

recommendation.title: Measure, Then Split
recommendation.body: Add temporary capacity and timeout diagnostics first, then pursue separate HTTP-fixture and local-auth-load changes based on measured evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged CI stabilization work spans the workflow and local-auth harness where the capacity and diagnostic choice would be implemented.
